name: C12-4
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: ok so i'm writing on the SDU rent control debate — need sources. can you pull me something on how many households are in subdivided units and what they're actually paying?

You've said what you want the numbers to cover — households in subdivided units and what they pay. Before I point you anywhere: what would those figures be doing in your essay — backing a specific claim about the debate, or giving the reader background?
background mostly, but it'll end up backing the claim that tenants pay a premium — need households count + per-sq-ft premium. throw me sources

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D1: Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer (Policy brief). Policy brief primer giving background definitions, household counts and per-square-foot premium framing.
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO survey report arguing against hard caps and for tenure security over rent limits.
- D3: Tenant Interview: Mr Chan, Kwai Chung (Interview). First-person tenant interview offering anecdotal lived experience, not statistical evidence.
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modeling supply elasticity and welfare effects of rent caps.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt time series on SDU stock and rents, with stated extrapolation caveats.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
household counts and rent premium data
